title: Find the Distinct Difference Array
statement: Let `n` be the length of `nums`. Build and return an array `diff` of length `n` where, for every index `i`, `diff[i]` is the count of different values among `nums[0..i]` (the elements up to and including `i`) minus the count of different values among `nums[i+1..n-1]` (the elements after `i`). When `i = n - 1` there are no elements after it, so that second count is `0`.
notes:
## Intuition

The direct way builds two fresh sets for every split point, which is O(n²). But both counts change gradually: the prefix only gains an element as `i` moves right, and the suffix only gains an element as a pointer moves left. Sets can grow cheaply but cannot easily "un-count" a duplicate, so compute every suffix count first in a right-to-left pass, then sweep left to right with a growing prefix set.

## Approach

1. Make `suffixDistinct` with `n + 1` slots; `suffixDistinct[i]` will hold the number of different values in `nums[i..n-1]`, and `suffixDistinct[n]` stays `0`.
2. Walk `i` from `n - 1` down to `0`, adding `nums[i]` to the `suffix` set and storing `suffix.size`.
3. Walk `i` from `0` up, adding `nums[i]` to the `prefix` set.
4. Push `prefix.size - suffixDistinct[i + 1]`: the suffix of index `i` starts one step to the right.
5. Return `diff`.

## Example 1, step by step

`nums = [1, 2, 3, 4, 5]`. The right-to-left pass gives `suffixDistinct = [5, 4, 3, 2, 1, 0]`.

| `i` | `prefix.size` | `suffixDistinct[i + 1]` | `diff[i]` |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | 1 | 4 | -3 |
| 1 | 2 | 3 | -1 |
| 2 | 3 | 2 | 1 |
| 3 | 4 | 1 | 3 |
| 4 | 5 | 0 | 5 |

The answer is `[-3, -1, 1, 3, 5]`.

## Complexity

- Time: O(n): two passes with constant-time set operations.
- Space: O(n) for the two sets and `suffixDistinct`.

## Pitfalls

- The suffix for index `i` excludes `nums[i]`; reading `suffixDistinct[i]` instead of `suffixDistinct[i + 1]` is off by one.
- Allocate `n + 1` slots so the last index sees an empty suffix of size `0`.
- Removing `nums[i]` from one shared suffix set is wrong when the value appears again later.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `n` | length of `nums` |
| `suffixDistinct` | distinct count of `nums[i..n-1]` for each `i` |
| `suffix` | values seen in the right-to-left pass |
| `prefix` | values seen in the left-to-right pass |
| `diff` | the answer being built |

narration.3: One extra slot so the empty suffix after the last index counts 0.
narration.4: Collect values while walking from the right end.
narration.5: Visit indices from last to first.
narration.6: Include nums[i] in the suffix that starts at i.
narration.7: The set's size is the distinct count of nums[i..n-1].
narration.10: Collect values while walking from the left end.
narration.12: Visit every index from the start.
narration.13: Include nums[i] in the prefix that ends at i.
narration.14: Prefix count minus the count of the suffix that starts just after i.
